newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Tuntex plans $2.8 bln Thai plants.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Tuntex plans $2.8 bln Thai plants.

text.p: Taiwan's Tuntex Distinct group said on Tuesday it would begin building two plants to make raw materials for polyester fibre production in Thailand in late 1997 with investment totalling US$2.8 billlion.
The group planned to invest $2 billion in building a paraxylene plant and $800 million in building a pure terephthalic acid (PTA) plant in Thailand, said Tuntex spokesman Chang Tsu-an.
"This is part of our plans in Thailand to have a vertical integration for our polyester fibre business," Chang told Reuters.
PTA is a raw material for producing polyester fibre. Paraxylene is a raw material for making PTA.
Tuntex group already has a Thai affiliate Tuntex Public (Thailand) Co, a polyester fibre producer, listed in Thailand's stock market.
The group's other Thai affiliate -- Tuntex Petrochemical (Thailand) Co, which produces PTA -- plans to be listed in the Thai stock market in June this year, Chang said.
Tuntex planned to start building the two plants by the end of this year, with completion seen in 2000, he said.
The paraxylene plant would be designed with an annual production capacity of 800,000 tonnes, while the PTA plant would have an annual capacity of 900,000 tonnes.
Tuntex Petrochemical already has one PTA production line in operation with an annual capacity of 420,000 tonnes, Chang said.
Tuntex is one of Taiwan's leading construction and chemical fibre makers.
